label: Configure subagent invocation context passing and spawning
model: claude-opus-5 (authored in a Claude Code session)

cards.front: What is the primary mechanism for spawning a subagent in the Claude Agent SDK, and what three things does the call carry?
cards.back: The Task tool. The orchestrator calls Task with (1) a description of the work, (2) an optional allowedTools set, and (3) any context the subagent needs. The SDK launches a fresh agent loop, runs it to completion, and returns the result to the orchestrator.

cards.front: What happens if you omit allowedTools when spawning a subagent?
cards.back: The subagent inherits ALL tools available in the environment — a common source of unintended side effects (e.g. a summarisation subagent that accidentally has shell execution). Always declare the minimal tool set: least privilege.

cards.front: Why is 'pass the context by shared global state' a design error for subagents?
cards.back: Subagents run in isolated loops with no access to the orchestrator's conversation history or globals. Anything the subagent needs — user intent, prior results, file contents, config — must appear explicitly in its initial messages array. Shared state fails silently and is hard to debug.

cards.front: You spawn several subagents that don't depend on each other. What is the mistake to avoid, and the fix?
cards.back: Mistake: awaiting them sequentially in a loop, wasting wall-clock time proportional to the number of agents. Fix: Promise.all for truly independent subagents, or Promise.allSettled when partial failures are acceptable.

cards.front: When should you spawn a subagent rather than doing the work in the main conversation?
cards.back: When a side task would flood the main context with material you won't reference again — search results, logs, bulk file contents. The subagent does that work in its own context window and returns only the summary. Define a custom subagent when you keep spawning the same kind of worker.

cards.front: In Claude Code, what does a subagent actually receive at launch?
cards.back: Its own context window with its custom system prompt and basic environment (e.g. working directory) — NOT the full Claude Code system prompt and NOT the parent conversation. It also has its own tool access and independent permissions.

cards.front: Which subagent frontmatter fields are required, and what does `tools` default to?
cards.back: Required: name (unique, lowercase+hyphens, no ':') and description (when Claude should delegate to it). `tools` is optional and defaults to inheriting all tools; `disallowedTools` subtracts from that. `model` defaults to `inherit`.

cards.front: What is the precedence order for subagent definitions, highest to lowest?
cards.back: 1. Managed settings (org-wide) → 2. --agents CLI flag (session) → 3. .claude/agents/ (project) → 4. ~/.claude/agents/ (user) → 5. plugin agents/ directory.

cards.front: How do you stop Claude Code from delegating at all, or block one specific subagent type?
cards.back: Deny the `Agent` tool itself in permissions.deny to prevent any delegation; add the specific built-in type to permissions.deny to block just that one.

cards.front: What is distinctive about the built-in Explore subagent?
cards.back: It is a fast, read-only codebase search agent with Write/Edit denied and thoroughness levels (quick / medium / very thorough). Explore and Plan skip CLAUDE.md and git status to stay fast and cheap; every other subagent loads both.
